metadata.title: Science Tutor Workshop Knowledge Base
metadata.notice: This bundled fallback contains original workshop questions for offline use.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a convergent plate boundary?

options.b: Two plates move toward each other.

questions.explanation: Convergent boundaries form where plates move toward one another.

questions.question: Which process most directly creates new oceanic crust at a mid-ocean ridge?
questions.explanation: At divergent boundaries, magma rises and cools to form new crust.

questions.question: A transform boundary is characterized mainly by plates that...
questions.explanation: Transform boundaries involve lateral motion of plates.

questions.question: What type of plate boundary forms when two plates move toward each other?
questions.explanation: Convergent boundaries form where plates move toward each other and compress the crust.

questions.question: Which process creates new oceanic crust at a divergent boundary?

options.a: New crust forming as plates separate

questions.explanation: At divergent boundaries, plates separate while magma rises and cools into new crust.

questions.question: Which boundary type is represented by the two plates moving in opposite directions along the fault?
questions.explanation: Transform boundaries involve plates sliding parallel to the boundary.

topics.name: Water Cycle
topics.description: Movement of water through Earth systems.

questions.question: Which process changes liquid water at Earth’s surface into water vapor?
questions.explanation: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapor.

questions.question: What happens during condensation?
questions.explanation: Condensation forms liquid droplets from water vapor.

questions.question: Which reservoir contains most of Earth’s liquid surface water?
questions.explanation: Oceans contain the vast majority of Earth’s surface water.

questions.question: Which water-cycle process moves water from clouds to Earth’s surface?
questions.explanation: Precipitation moves water from clouds to Earth’s surface.

questions.question: What process describes water moving downhill across the land surface?
questions.explanation: Surface runoff is water flowing downslope toward streams, lakes, or oceans.

questions.question: What is the downward movement of water into soil called?
questions.explanation: Infiltration is the movement of surface water into soil.

questions.question: Which process transports weathered sediment from one place to another?
questions.explanation: Erosion is the transport of weathered material.

questions.question: Deposition occurs when transported sediment...

options.b: settles out of the transporting medium.

questions.explanation: Deposition occurs when sediments are dropped or settle.

questions.question: Which agent can cause both erosion and deposition?
questions.explanation: Flowing water can erode, transport, and deposit sediment.

questions.question: Where is erosion usually strongest in a river meander?
questions.explanation: The outside of a bend typically has faster flow and stronger erosion.

questions.question: Why does a river delta form where a river enters a larger body of water?

options.a: The river speeds up and removes all sediment.
options.b: The river slows and deposits sediment.
options.c: The water turns into vapor instantly.

questions.explanation: Reduced flow velocity allows sediment to settle and accumulate.

questions.question: Which process describes sediment settling out of moving water?
questions.explanation: Deposition occurs when transported sediment settles.

topics.name: Cells
topics.description: Cell structures and transport across membranes.

questions.question: Which structure contains most of a eukaryotic cell’s genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains most of the cell’s DNA.

questions.question: Which organelle is strongly associated with cellular respiration and ATP production?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are central to aerobic cellular respiration.

questions.question: Which structure is present in plant cells but not animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall outside the membrane.

questions.question: Which cell structure contains most of a eukaryotic cell’s genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains most of a eukaryotic cell’s DNA.

questions.question: Which organelle in plant cells is associated with photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which process is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane.

topics.name: Ecosystems
topics.description: Energy flow and interactions in ecosystems.

questions.question: In a food chain, producers obtain energy most directly from...
questions.explanation: Most ecosystems ultimately depend on solar energy captured by producers.

questions.question: What is the main role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Decomposers return nutrients to the ecosystem.

questions.question: Which is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Water is nonliving and therefore abiotic.

questions.question: In a food chain where a rabbit is eaten by a snake, which organism receives energy directly from the rabbit?
questions.explanation: Energy moves from the rabbit to the snake that eats it.

questions.question: Which level of the energy pyramid contains the greatest amount of available energy?
questions.explanation: Energy is greatest at the producer level and decreases upward.

questions.question: Which of these is an abiotic factor in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Water is a nonliving environmental factor.

topics.name: Forces and Motion
topics.description: Net force, balanced forces, and motion.

questions.question: If the net force on an object is zero, its motion...
questions.explanation: Zero net force means no acceleration; velocity remains constant.

questions.question: Newton’s second law relates acceleration to...
questions.explanation: Newton’s second law is commonly expressed as F = ma.

questions.question: Which quantity includes both magnitude and direction?
questions.explanation: Force is a vector quantity.

questions.question: What is the net horizontal force when 50 N acts left and 50 N acts right?
questions.explanation: Equal 50 N forces in opposite directions cancel.

questions.question: If the net force on an object points right, in which direction will it accelerate?
questions.explanation: The larger force is to the right, so the net force points right.

questions.question: What does a straight rising line on a position-time graph indicate?
questions.explanation: A linear position-time graph has constant slope, which means constant velocity.
